analysis_method: Native iperf3 receiver sum_received is authoritative; retransmissions are sender sum_sent. Before/after router snapshots bracket each run and include intervening background traffic. No counters were cleared. One TCP stream,30s paced850M or60s uncapped; one additional30s four-stream diagnostic in initial host phase. Both endpoints share a VM but are isolated by network namespace; route/TTL/MAC proof confirms router traversal.
interpretation: After the owner restored the VM to the 10G host, C delivered849.994Mbps paced on port7,940.084/941.472Mbps uncapped on port7,850.018Mbps paced on port8, and9.163/9.296Gbps uncapped on port8. These short results are comparable with B.

Initial2.300/2.301Gbps and four-stream2.319Gbps measurements remain preserved. The host move removed that ceiling without a router firmware, correction or tuning change. This supports a host/path limitation; the precise physical limiting component was not independently inventoried.

No sampled CRC/input/output errors or output drops, CPP restart, missed keepalive or send error. Nonzero TCP retransmissions remain; background QFP/unknown-protocol counters are separately recorded. Neither a loss-free network nor the location of every retransmission is established.

The10G test routes VLAN5↔83 through one physical10G trunk. It is not two-port10G qualification, simultaneous bidirectional capacity, or an hour/overnight loaded stability test. TPM and standby12V warnings remain unresolved.
